newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks end broadly lower, techs slide.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks end broadly lower, techs slide.

text.p: Wall Street stocks ended lower on Wednesday, weighed down by higher interest rates and a continued stiff sell-off in technology shares.

The Dow industrials fell 19 points to close unofficially at 6878, a moderate decline given the broad weakness that saw technology and transportation stocks tumble and interest rates creep towards six-month highs.
"We're nearly at seven percent on the long bond and we're certainly not going to make much progress while that's the case," said Harry Laubscher, market analyst at Tucker Anthony.
"For now, people seem very concerned about next week's (Federal Reserve) meeting," Laubscher said.
Contributing to the worries about interest rates was a 0.3 percent rise in the February Consumer Price Index (CPI), up from 0.1 percent in January. Economists had forecast a 0.2 percent increase.
While the slightly higher reading was not greeted with alarm, economists said the data failed to show sufficient weakness to change the unusually uncertain outlook for next week's Fed meeting.

"The February CPI report won't change any minds about what the Fed will do at the March 25 meeting," Bruce Steinberg, manager of macroeconomics at Merrill Lynch said. "We expect the Fed to leave policy unchanged, but we admit it is almost a 50-50 call at this point."

While Wall Street remains divided on the outlook for interest rates, its attitude appears far clearer regarding technology stocks, which have endured an extended sell-off since peaking in late January.
That trend continued today, with the Nasdaq Composite declining to its lowest level since early November, 1996.
The decline appeared to gain momentum today, hitting a wide variety of tech stocks. Networking, semiconductor and computer makers all finished with heavy losses.
Intel Corp fell 3-3/8 to 133-3/8, Ascend Communications Inc fell 2-3/8 to 45-3/4, International Business Machines Corp dipped 1-1/2 to 137-7/8 and Microsoft Corp slipped 2-7/8 to 96-3/4.

"Everyone who wanted to sell is sold," said Gary Kaltbaum, director of technical research at J.W. Charles Securities Inc. "I think we're bottoming for a bounce, but that said, I don't know how well we're going to bounce."
Also hit hard were transportation stocks, which backtracked sharply from their recent rally.

The Dow Jones Transportation Average tumbled 51.17 points to 2418.42, led lower by Burlington Northern Santa Fe Corp, which fell 3-7/8 to 78-1/2 after the railroad company warned of weak first quarter results.
Airlines also finished lower, hit by profit-taking and rising fuel costs. Delta Air Lines Inc fell 3-1/4 to 84-1/2 and United Airlines parent company UAL Corp shed 2-1/4 to 68-1/4.
In individual issues, Adobe Systems Inc jumped 4-1/8 to 39, bucking the trend in tech stocks. The company reported first quarter earnings late yesterday that were stronger than analysts had expected.

Lexmark International Group Inc fell 3-7/8 to 23-7/8. The company, a maker of printers and related products, said its first quarter earnings would meet analysts' estimates but revenues would fall short of expectations.
The S&P 500 index fell 3.89 points to 785.77.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 20.05 points to 1249.29.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
